clue.text: The principal pain?

parts.note: the principal part of the body is the head, so its pain is literally a pain there; the surface suggests the chief or worst of one's troubles

explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the head is the ordinary sense, and the word is also used for whatever is the chief nuisance.

clue.text: Posy she made up mostly from these little blue flowers

indicators.note: made up means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, so the final letter of she is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A posy someone has assembled consists largely of small blue blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SHE to SH; 'made up' rearranges POSY + SH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb of the mint family bearing spikes of small blue flowers.

clue.text: Vinegar may lead to acute suffering

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the lead of a word is its opening letter, so the start of may is taken

explanation.surface: Drinking vinegar might bring on a sharp attack of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' takes M from 'may'; 'suffering' rearranges M + ACUTE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetum is the Latin and pharmacy term for vinegar, the source of the word acetic.

clue.text: Union obtaining a nice settlement after all

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the word all in the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a settlement is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A marriage that settles happily after everything has been said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests marriage, but this is a pact; 'settlement' gives IANCE and 'after' puts it behind the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit, as between nations or families.

clue.text: Blow of petulance

definitions.meaning: to puff out air, as in the wolf who will ... and puff
a fit of sulky offence, as when someone goes off in a sulk

explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out heavily is one sense; a bout of peevish annoyance is the other, so both senses fit the single word.

clue.text: Match seen at a cricket club on ring road

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricket fixture is watched at a club beside the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a cricket game, but it is a verb: to agree or correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to agree or correspond, which is what things do when they match.

clue.text: A pound for a horse

parts.note: the surface reads as a price paid for a horse, but pound means an enclosure for animals

explanation.definitionFit: A corral is a pen or enclosure for horses and cattle, an animal pound in the American West.

clue.text: Defeated, arrived by air

definitions.meaning: beat or got the better of an opponent
split as came over, the way a flight crosses to reach its destination

explanation.definitionFit: Overcome means beat in the past tense, and the same letters split as came over describe travelling across in flight.

clue.text: Badly glued racket held responsible for misguiding

indicators.note: held means the noise is clasped inside the rearranged letters
badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: a din is a loud racket or noise

explanation.surface: Poorly glued items making a noise are blamed for leading someone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' is noise, not a bat; 'Badly' gives DELUG, which 'held' splits around the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Deluding someone means leading them into a false belief, that is misleading them.

clue.text: Let fly, is whirling — to become a star

indicators.note: whirling suggests spinning about, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrower lets the ball go with a spin, hoping for stardom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling' rearranges LETFLYIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stellify is, in poetic use, to turn into or place among the stars, that is to be raised to the heavens.

clue.text: Blair's banker

definitions.meaning: Eric Blair wrote under a pen name, so this is what Blair is better known as
in crosswords a banker is something with banks, a river; this one flows through Suffolk

explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of the writer Eric Blair, and the Orwell is also a river in Suffolk, England.

clue.text: Originates in airways

parts.note: taken as written
vents are openings or passages that let air through

explanation.surface: A process begins inside the passages of the lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airways' suggests breathing tubes or airlines, but here it means ducts for air.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent is to originate or devise something new.

clue.text: Comical juvenile lead not to be seen — due to this trouble?

indicators.note: not to be seen means a letter vanishes from the word

parts.note: jocular means joking or comical

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter, here the start of juvenile

explanation.surface: A funny young star of the stage keeps out of sight because of some eye complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: JOCULAR loses its J, the 'lead' of 'juvenile'. The definition works with the rest: not being seen due to ocular trouble, 'this' standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eyes, so ocular trouble is eye trouble, a reason for not seeing.

clue.text: Extended each end, redesigned to hold an indefinite number

indicators.note: to hold means the rearranged letters take in another piece
redesigned means given a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the mathematician's symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A rod was lengthened at both ends after a redesign to carry an unspecified quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges EACH END to ENHACED; 'to hold' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhanced means increased or augmented, made greater in extent or value.

clue.text: Engineers lined up, we hear, then set free

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers of the British Army, plural REs

indicators.note: we hear means a word is said aloud and spelt as another that sounds the same

parts.note: queued means stood in a line

explanation.surface: Engineers stood in line and were then released.
explanation.walkthrough: The REs are soldiers of the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps. 'we hear' gives CUED, which sounds like QUEUED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to set them free from danger or captivity; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Intrigued by church in home counties, by the sea

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for church sits inside the letters for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East of England, SE
the Med is the Mediterranean, the sea

explanation.surface: Someone plotted from a church near London and from the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the South East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To scheme is to plot or intrigue, so schemed is intrigued as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: State female's to be guillotined

indicators.note: guillotining takes off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a woman is a female; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A government announces that a woman will be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: WOMAN loses its first letter W when 'guillotined'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a country, a sovereign state, on the south-east coast of the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: One result of bowling away on a brief holiday?

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Bowling might be one outcome of a short trip away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off-break is a ball that turns sharply after bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-break is a delivery in cricket that spins from the off side, something a bowler produces.

clue.text: Flush job for the water engineer?

definitions.meaning: flush means having plenty of money, rich
split as three words, a well is something a water engineer has to do

explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means being wealthy, prosperous; and a well to do is a task for someone digging for water.

clue.text: Official's lame, and awkward when crossing a river

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters span the river, which goes inside them
awkward means clumsy or ill-arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official is lame and finds it hard to get across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lame' looks like a description of the official but is fodder; 'awkward' gives ALDEMAN, which 'crossing' opens for the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a borough or county council, a civic official.

clue.text: Bend a cable

definitions.meaning: to bend a limb or joint
an insulated electric cable on an appliance

explanation.definitionFit: To bend a muscle or limb is one sense; the British word for a lead or cord carrying electricity to an appliance is the other.

clue.text: Cutlets prepared to make a dash for it!

indicators.note: prepared like food in a kitchen, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The cutlets have been cooked, and someone races off with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CUTLETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle is to run with short quick steps, to hurry away.

clue.text: Believe bird's getting a lift from a donkey

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the word, so it is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A bird is said to have hitched a ride on a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a lift' turns EMU into UME, placed below ASS in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose or take something to be true, to believe it.

clue.text: The others pop in for a meal

indicators.note: in places the word for father inside the word for the others

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
pa and pop are both informal names for a father

explanation.surface: The rest of the family drop in for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like a verb (drop in), but it is a noun, father.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, a formal and old-fashioned word for one.

clue.text: Valiant charioteer coming a cropper, sheds tear

indicators.note: coming a cropper means taking a bad fall, so the letters are tumbled into disorder
sheds means casts off, so these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A chariot driver crashes and weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming a cropper' (British for a heavy fall) scrambles CHARIOTEER; 'sheds' takes away the letters of TEAR, leaving CHRIOE to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic means brave and bold, like a hero, which is what valiant means.

clue.text: Boastful talk about a pillar of support

indicators.note: about means the boastful word is placed around the letter A

parts.note: bluster is loud, empty, boastful talk

explanation.surface: Someone brags about being a mainstay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pillar of support' sounds figurative, a dependable person, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short posts that hold up a handrail, a small column bearing a load.

clue.text: Fair rise renegotiated incorporates it

indicators.note: incorporates means contains within, so the answer is found inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A reasonable pay rise was agreed in fresh talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective for the pay rise, but it is the definition, as in calm weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene weather is fair, calm and clear.

clue.text: To provide satisfaction, be sure to put on this suit

annotationWithheld.clue: To provide satisfaction, be sure to put on this suit

clue.text: Book for the flight

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
a mass departure of people fleeing a place

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book tells of the Israelites leaving Egypt, and the word also means any mass departure or escape.

clue.text: Pains starting trouble with back — result, climber in bed

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of pains is taken

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Back pain starts, and in the end the gardener's climbing plant is in its bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber in bed' is a plant in a flower bed, not a person in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a climbing shrub with pale blue flowers, grown in a garden bed.

clue.text: Money provided by monarch — one seen in luxury vehicle

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, a monarch

indicators.note: seen in means the word one sits inside the letters for the car

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, a luxury car
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king hands out cash while sitting in a limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: RR stands for Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: Kroner are the units of currency of Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Somehow I get my first hundred — an attractive result

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters come out in an unspecified new order
first means the opening letter of my

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches a first century, which pleases the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges I GET + M + C + AN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic means having the power to attract, as a magnet draws iron.
